english.title: Permit use of a vehicle to kill / take a wild bird
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), knowingly permitted the use of a mechanically propelled vehicle, namely **(..SPECIFY VEHICLE MAKE AND INDEX NUMBER..), in immediate pursuit of

(A)_[a wild bird,]_
(B)_[wild birds,]_

namely **(..SPECIFY WILD BIRD..), for the purpose of killing or taking

(C)_[it]_
(D)_[them]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 5(1)(f) and 21(1) of the Wildlife and Countryside Act 1981.

english.notes:
(i) See Section 27 for meaning of "wild bird".
(ii) See Section 21(6) for the forfeiture provisions.
(iii) See Section 21(7) for place where offence deemed to have been committed for jurisdiction purposes.
(iv) As amended by paragraph 10 of Schedule 12 to the Countryside and Rights of Way Act 2000.
(v) See offence wording H4585.

other.penalty:
Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Where more than one bird is involved in a single offence the maximum fine shall be determined as if the person convicted had been convicted of a separate offence in respect of each bird (Section 21(5)).

Time limit for prosecutions:
Complex - see legislation

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
